# International Journal of Language & Communication Disorders

## Overview

The **International Journal of Language & Communication Disorders (IJLCD)** is a peer-reviewed academic journal dedicated to publishing research in the fields of speech, language, and communication disorders. It is one of the leading and most respected journals in the discipline of speech-language pathology and related fields.

---

## Key Details

### Publisher and Affiliation
- Published by **Wiley-Blackwell** on behalf of the **Royal College of Speech & Language Therapists (RCSLT)**
- The RCSLT is the professional body for speech and language therapists in the United Kingdom
- The journal serves as an important publication outlet for both UK-based and international researchers

### ISSN
- **Print ISSN:** 1368-2822
- **Electronic ISSN:** 1460-6984

### History
- The journal has roots going back several decades
- It was previously known as the **British Journal of Disorders of Communication**, which was established in **1966**
- It was renamed to the **International Journal of Language & Communication Disorders** in **1999**, reflecting its broader international scope
- The name change also signaled an effort to attract research from across the world rather than primarily UK-based work

---

## Scope and Focus

The journal covers a wide range of topics related to:

### Clinical Areas
- Speech sound disorders (articulation and phonological disorders)
- Language disorders in children and adults
- Stuttering and fluency disorders
- Voice disorders
- Acquired communication disorders (e.g., aphasia, dysarthria, apraxia of speech)
- Augmentative and alternative communication (AAC)
- Swallowing disorders (dysphagia)
- Autism spectrum disorder and associated communication difficulties
- Developmental language disorder (DLD)
- Traumatic brain injury and communication
- Dementia and communication
- Hearing impairment and its impact on communication

### Research Areas
- Assessment and diagnosis of communication disorders
- Intervention and treatment efficacy and effectiveness
- Theoretical models of language and communication
- Epidemiology of communication disorders
- Service delivery and clinical practice
- Psychosocial aspects of communication disorders
- Neuroscience underpinnings of communication

---

## Types of Articles Published

The journal typically publishes:

- **Original research articles** (quantitative and qualitative studies)
- **Systematic reviews and meta-analyses**
- **Clinical reports and case studies**
- **Theoretical and conceptual papers**
- **Methodological papers**
- **Review articles**
- **Letters to the editor**
- **Editorials and commentaries**
- **Special issues** focused on specific topics

---

## Audience

The journal is aimed at:
- Speech-language pathologists/therapists (SLPs/SLTs)
- Researchers in linguistics, communication sciences, and disorders
- Psychologists
- Neurologists and other medical professionals
- Educators and clinical supervisors
- Audiologists
- Policy makers in health and education

---

## Impact and Reputation

- The journal holds a respectable **Impact Factor** within its field (the specific impact factor changes year to year; it has generally been in the range of approximately **2–3** in recent years, though this should be verified with current data)
- It is indexed in major databases including:
  - **PubMed/MEDLINE**
  - **CINAHL**
  - **PsycINFO**
  - **Scopus**
  - **Web of Science**
  - **ERIC**
- It is considered a high-quality journal within speech-language pathology and communication sciences
- It is frequently cited in clinical practice guidelines and research

---

## Editorial Structure

- The journal is overseen by an **Editor-in-Chief** supported by an **editorial board** comprising international experts in speech, language, and communication disorders
- Manuscripts undergo **double-blind peer review** in most cases
- The editorial board typically represents diverse geographic regions and subdisciplines within the field

---

## Special Features

- The journal has published influential **special issues** on topics such as:
  - Developmental Language Disorder (DLD)
  - Evidence-based practice in speech-language therapy
  - Social communication
  - Aphasia
  - Multilingualism and communication disorders
- It often publishes **consensus statements** and **position papers** relevant to the profession
- The journal has been associated with efforts to promote **evidence-based practice** in speech-language therapy

---

## Open Access

- The journal offers **Open Access** options for authors, consistent with Wiley's open access policies
- Authors can pay an **Article Publication Charge (APC)** to make their work freely available
- It also complies with various **funder mandates** regarding open access publication

---

## Relationship with RCSLT

- As the official journal of the Royal College of Speech & Language Therapists, it plays an important role in:
  - Disseminating research relevant to UK clinical practice
  - Informing professional standards and guidelines
  - Supporting continuing professional development for SLTs in the UK and beyond

---

## Notable Contributions to the Field

- The journal has been a key outlet for research on **Developmental Language Disorder**, particularly following efforts to standardize terminology in the field (associated with researchers like Dorothy Bishop)
- It has published foundational research on assessment tools, therapy approaches, and clinical frameworks used in practice today
- Research published in the journal has informed national and international clinical guidelines

---

## Submission and Publication Process

- Authors submit manuscripts through an **online submission system** (typically ScholarOne/Manuscript Central via Wiley)
- The journal has specific **author guidelines** regarding formatting, word limits, ethical requirements, and referencing style
- Typical sections required include: abstract, introduction, methods, results, discussion, and references
- Ethical approval and participant consent documentation are typically required for clinical research

---

## Summary

The International Journal of Language & Communication Disorders is a **prestigious, internationally recognized peer-reviewed journal** that has made substantial contributions to the science and practice of speech-language pathology over many decades. Its affiliation with the RCSLT and its broad international scope make it a key resource for clinicians, researchers, and educators working in the field of communication disorders worldwide.

---

*Note: Specific details such as current impact factor, current editor-in-chief, and exact submission guidelines may change over time, so it is advisable to consult the journal's official website or Wiley's platform for the most up-to-date information.*
